items.q: What can't an MCP server tell today?
items.a: Whether the **user or the agent** actually made the request.

items.q: How do agents usually get access today?
items.a: Through users' **personal access tokens**, static keys and **over-privileged service accounts**.

items.q: Why are agents worse than an unlocked laptop?
items.a: They act with your credentials **all the time**, and they're **non-deterministic**.

items.q: What identity should an agent have?
items.a: Its **own identity**, even per session, **separate from the user** who launched it.

items.q: What kind of credentials should agents get?
items.a: **Short-lived, scoped** tokens per interaction via **OAuth**, never a master key.
Which users can use **which agents**, and which agents can act **on whose behalf**.

items.q: Which policies and records are required?
items.a: Policies for **which actions need human approval**, plus an **audit trail**.
In a **vault behind a gateway**, out of the agent's reach.

items.q: What can a gateway do that coarse legacy scopes can't?
items.a: **Attenuate** requests, like allowing reading mail but **blocking sending**.

items.q: What does routing every call through a gateway give you?
What are the costs of a gateway?
items.a: Extra **latency**, a **high-value target** and TLS and routing complexity.
